parsed.explanation: No trans-specific statute and no documented near-certain imprisonment on sight, so it sits above the 0.15 tier. But the state is itself the documented perpetrator against gender-nonconforming people: interior-ministry power to deport foreign nationals 'disturbing public order or morality' applied to travellers perceived as queer without any charge (incidents through 2022), police entrapment via dating apps naming trans women as particular targets, blackmail, arrests, coerced anal examinations and abuse inside police stations. The sex-work/morality statute supplies prison sentences and is documented as a lever against this population, not a dead letter. Recourse is absent (no anti-discrimination law; complaints unaddressed), and the 2023-2026 legal analyses confirm the machinery remains operative, even though the latest dated forced-examination case is 2017. Border marker-screening is unresolved but not needed to reach this level. Comparable to the police-coercion tier, short of routine imprisonment.
